faqs.q: What should I include on a moving company quote?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and DOT number, the client, move-from and move-to addresses, dated line items (crew labor, truck and fuel, surcharges, packing, valuation), a valid-until date, deposit terms and whether the quote is binding or non-binding. Interstate moves are regulated by FMCSA.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate the deposit and balance automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, 25% deposit and balance due update automatically.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your moving authority and a CPA or attorney before use.

deepDive.heading: Moving quotes: what makes an estimate binding
deepDive.sub: A moving quote is only as good as its estimate type and the survey behind it. Customers compare bottom-line numbers from quotes that are not comparable at all.

paras: A binding estimate fixes the price regardless of actual weight — which means the mover carries the risk of a heavier shipment, and usually prices that risk in. A non-binding estimate is a professional guess, and the final invoice follows actual weight and services. A not-to-exceed estimate caps the bill at the quoted figure but still charges less if the shipment is lighter.

The quote must say which one it is, in terms the customer can understand, on the same page as the number. Most quote disputes are not about the price but about which kind of price the customer thought they had.

blocks.h3: The survey decides whether the quote holds
paras: An in-home or video survey is what separates a real estimate from a phone guess. Weight estimates are driven by furniture volume, box count, and the awkward items — pianos, safes, gym equipment, large appliances. A quote given without a survey should say so explicitly, and should be priced as a range rather than a number.

Where the customer declines the survey, note it on the quote and record what was assumed: three-bedroom house, approximately 8,000 lb, two flights of stairs. Assumptions written down are what let a mover re-quote honestly when the load turns out larger.

Most quotes carry conditions, and they should be on the document: the quote assumes first-floor or elevator access at both ends, a truck parkable within 75 feet, no packing service, and the inventory listed. If the customer adds a flight of stairs, a storage-in-transit period, or 20 more boxes, the quote is re-priced — legitimately.

The failure mode is the quote that lists none of this and then adds charges on the day. Those are the disputes that reach the FMCSA and the state regulator, and they are almost always caused by an incomplete quote rather than a dishonest invoice.

Interstate movers may not collect more than 10 percent before the move date under federal rules, and many states impose their own limits on local moves. Whatever the deposit is, state it on the quote along with the cancellation window and any refund terms. A quote that omits both invites a customer to assume neither exists.
